content:
alice.m: Heads up - production hit a spike of unwrap failures for envelope-encrypted payloads around 08:12 UTC. Start of thread.

bob.ops: saw it. errors: `403` from AKV during DEK unwrap, service reports `Key not authorized` for key version.

carla.sec: @bob.ops can you paste logs? we need to know whether this is RBAC or rotation.

bob.ops: logs: ```2026-03-19T08:12:31Z ERROR unwrap failed: status=403, body={"error":{"code":"Forbidden","message":"Access denied to key version"}}```

sam.platform: quick context: we use AKV to wrap DEKs (envelope encryption). KEK is a customer-shared key in AKV, DEKs stored encrypted in object store. Redwood runtime caches unwrapped DEKs for 1h.

ajay.sre: were key operations (unwrapKey) explicitly allowed for the MI? we recently moved from access policies to RBAC.

bob.ops: looks like the tenant had an RBAC migration yesterday evening. I remember a script toggled `Key Vault -> Access policies` off and assigned `Key Vault Crypto Officer` role at subscription scope.

carla.sec: RBAC vs access policies is the usual suspect. RBAC needs `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/unwrap/action` identity permission via role assignment on the key resource or vault. Also note cross-tenant service principals behave differently.

alice.m: timeline: 20:30 yesterday RBAC migration; 08:12 failures today when rate of unwrapping spiked with cold cache after deploy.

sam.platform: reproduction: I ran `az rest` to call unwrap with our MI token and got the same 403.

bob.ops: command snippet we used to test: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://myvault.vault.azure.net/keys/kek/1234567890abcdef/unwrap?api-version=7.4 -d '{"alg":"RSA-OAEP","value":"..."}'```

ajay.sre: interesting: role assignment exists at subscription but RBAC checks resource type. If the assignment scope doesn't include the key's specific resourceId (e.g., when key was re-created), Azure may block. check `az role assignment list --assignee <mi>` and the key resourceId.

carla.sec: confirm also that the MI's token audience is `https://vault.azure.net`. We've seen tokens for `https://management.azure.com/` mistakenly used and get inscrutable denies.

bob.ops: token looks correct. `az account get-access-token --resource=https://vault.azure.net` returned a token, same 403 on unwrap.

alice.m: root cause hypothesis: RBAC migration changed how role assignments were scoped; key version rotated/recreated during rotation process, and role assignment didn’t propagate to new key resource id.

sam.platform: mitigation idea: grant `Key Vault Crypto User` or `Key Vault Crypto Service` on vault level to the MI as a stopgap (broad scope) so unwraps succeed until we fix fine-grained assignments.

carla.sec: agree. but we must document the least-priv path. For production: role at vault scope with `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/*` unwrap allowed. For stricter: role at key resource id with that key id.

ajay.sre: runbook steps (short):
1) verify failing principal: `az role assignment list --assignee <mi-principal-id>`
2) verify key resource id: `az keyvault key show --vault-name myvault --name kek --query id`
3) if role missing, create assignment: `az role assignment create --role "Key Vault Crypto User" --assignee <mi> --scope <key-resource-id>`
4) optionally, assign at vault level: `--scope /subscriptions/..../resourceGroups/..../providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/myvault`

bob.ops: performed assignment at vault level as emergency patch. unwraps recovered at 08:30.

alice.m: good. postmortem action items?

carla.sec: checklist:
- add alert: `unwrap 403` rate > threshold -> P1
- audit script: post-RBAC-migration validate role assignments for all MIs consuming keys (compare `az role assignment list` vs list of MIs in manifest)
- add unit test in deploy pipeline: simulate MI unwrap after RBAC toggles

sam.platform: also recommend key-rotation safety: when automating key rotation, create new key version under same key id (use `az keyvault key create --kty RSA --size 2048 --vault-name myvault --name kek`) so role assignments remain valid. Avoid delete/recreate which changes resource id.

ajay.sre: additional hardening:
- implement client-side exponential backoff + small caching of unwrap failures to avoid thundering impact on AKV.
- add fallback unwrap via secondary key (if cross-tenant fallback allowed)

carla.sec: logging: enable Key Vault diagnostic settings -> send `AzureDiagnostics` to Log Analytics or event hub and retain 90 days. That gives `OperationName_s` and `ResultType` for forensic analysis.

bob.ops: noted a log entry that helped: ```OperationName_s: UnwrapKey; ResultType: 403; CallerIp_s: 52.174.23.1; CallerObjectId_g: xxxxx```

alice.m: security note: AKV never returns plaintext DEKs in audit logs. but ensure storage access logs are correlated to know when unwrapped DEK was used.

sam.platform: perf note: unwrap latency is ~40-80ms from eu-west. Caching DEKs for common prefixes reduces token expense and tail latency. We should tune cache TTL and prefetch on deploy.

carla.sec: follow-ups for compliance: record change control entry for RBAC migration and include post-change validation checklist.

ajay.sre: action assignments: @bob.ops emergency role assignment done and reverted to vault-level emergency scope. @sam.platform will run validation script to create per-key role assignments and add CI test. @carla.sec will create alert and update runbook. @alice.m will draft postmortem.

devops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0319-01, severity P2 -> assigned to eng-sre.

security-bot: Reminder: rotate KEKs per org policy. Next scheduled rotation window: 2026-04-01.

alice.m: thanks team. keep thread updated if anything else pops up.

bob.ops: adding notes to runbook with exact `az` commands and example debug output. will push later today.

carla.sec: great. closing for now unless more errors replicate. :thumbsup:
